history.effectiveDateNote: Took effect upon enactment on October 11, 1996 (no separate effective-date postponement clause in Pub. L. 104-292, § 2).
history.crsSummary: False Statements Accountability Act of 1996 — Restructures 18 U.S.C. § 1001 into subsections (a), (b), and (c) to apply false statement prohibitions across the executive, legislative, and judicial branches while exempting statements submitted by a party or counsel to a judge or magistrate in a judicial proceeding and limiting legislative branch coverage to administrative matters and congressional investigations.
history.enactedTextExcerpt: SEC. 2. RESTORING FALSE STATEMENTS PROHIBITION. Section 1001 of title 18, United States Code, is amended to read as follows: '§ 1001. Statements or entries generally (a) Except as otherwise provided in this section, whoever, in any matter within the jurisdiction of the executive, legislative, or judicial branch of the Government of the United States, knowingly and willfully— (1) falsifies, conceals, or covers up by any trick, scheme, or device a material fact; (2) makes any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or representation; or (3) makes or uses any false writing or document knowing the same to contain any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or entry; shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.'

history.effectiveDateNote: Enacted December 17, 2004 (Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004, § 6703(a)).
history.crsSummary: Increases the maximum term of imprisonment under 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a) from 5 years to 8 years if the offense involves international or domestic terrorism (as defined in 18 U.S.C. § 2331).
history.enactedTextExcerpt: SEC. 6703. ENHANCED PENALTY FOR FALSE STATEMENTS IN TERRORISM INVESTIGATIONS. Section 1001(a) of title 18, United States Code, is amended in the matter following paragraph (3) by inserting 'or, if the offense involves international or domestic terrorism (as defined in section 2331), imprisoned not more than 8 years,' after 'not more than 5 years,'.
